Why the three traditional pictures overlap

evidence.excerpt: See, for example, Lycan (1988, 2012) and, for a book-length defense of explanatory coherentism, Poston (2014).
A more substantial contrasting proposal is that what justifies our beliefs is ultimately the way in which they hang together or dovetail so as to produce a coherent set.

Since a coherence theory, in its basic form, does not assign any essential role to experience, there is little reason to think that a coherent system of belief will accurately reflect the external world.
But this observation, of course, thoroughly undermines any claim suggesting that coherence is indicative of truth.
And antecedently, the probability of what is reported may also be small.

He writes, in his discussion of reports from memory, that “[i]f … there were no initial presumption attaching to the mnemically presented … then no extent of congruity with other such items would give rise to any eventual credibility” (357).
For an elaboration of this point the reader is referred to Olsson (2005, 65), footnote 4.

sources.annotation: Explains holistic justification, competing coherence measures, and the precise limits of claims connecting coherence with truth.

evidence.excerpt: Perhaps the most interesting recent development in relation to Pyrrhonian Skepticism is that more and more epistemologists are arguing that the proper way to reply to Agrippa’s trilemma is to combine some of the positions that, for ease of exposition, we have presented as mutually exclusive.
